references.text: Mary sat at Jesus' feet and listened to his words—to sit at someone's feet is an expression of being a disciple. The demon-possessed man from the region of the Gerasenes was found sitting at Jesus' feet after being healed.
John's Gospel identifies Mary and Martha as sisters from Bethany, providing further background on the family that Jesus visited.
Mary fell at Jesus' feet when she met him after Lazarus' death, showing her characteristic attitude of devotion at Jesus' feet.
Mary anointed Jesus' feet with costly nard ointment and wiped them with her hair—again we see her at Jesus' feet in a posture of devotion and worship.
Paul describes how he was trained at Gamaliel's feet, illustrating the Jewish tradition of sitting at a teacher's feet as a sign of discipleship—the same position Mary took at Jesus' feet.
Moses describes how the people sat at the Lord's feet to receive his words—an image of the same attitude Mary showed when she sat at Jesus' feet to listen to his teaching.
Jesus defends Mary's choice and says that she has chosen the good portion which will not be taken from her—this confirms the value of listening to Jesus' words.
The young Jesus was found in the temple, sitting among the teachers and listening to them—a similar image of sitting and listening to learn.
Wisdom speaks of the blessed one who listens at her doors and watches by her doorposts—Mary chose to listen to Wisdom herself when she sat at Jesus' feet.
